borderline.why: B plans 'show stills for the look' but never ties the stills to the hardest frames or to viewing size, so a lenient grader could pass it.
C gives four ceilings that sum to $400 plus an approval rule, but 'what it buys' is only the category name and fallbacks are scattered prose with none for effects.
C plans stills and a silent rough cut, but its only approval gate before production is the written treatment and nothing says James sees them to choose.
C's clause on 'any future intended distribution, including commercial and perpetual use' could be read as marking uses unresolved, but it asks nothing and omits paid promotion, countries and term.
D commits to 'four representative styleframes' and review at 'actual viewing size', which covers not-only-a-hero-frame and size, but never names terminal text as the hardest frame.
